summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and a history of TIPS and recurrent liver cancer, was admitted for hematemesis and chest pain. He had been off his pantoprazole for 10 days, which likely contributed to upper GI bleeding from portal hypertensive gastropathy and esophagitis. He underwent a TIPS revision with balloon angioplasty, reducing the portosystemic gradient from 15 to 10 mmHg, and embolization of a gastric varix. A large-volume paracentesis removed 5 liters of fluid, with no signs of infection. He received one unit of packed red blood cells, and his hemoglobin stabilized. Chest pain was attributed to esophagitis and a hiatal hernia, with no cardiac cause. Hyponatremia remained stable on fluid restriction. He improved clinically, was discharged home on pantoprazole twice daily and sucralfate, with follow-up planned with hepatology and palliative care.
